utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, madam. The accused, the same advisory as always. Any time you're not receiving interpretation, please alert us straight away. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. I failed to say it yesterday that our legal assistant Ms. Verena Juebner is with us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And welcome, madam. Any further comments? I see you've got a member of your team missing, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan and Mr. Nicholls are out of the court working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So today we will have somewhat different schedule. We will -- we need to finish at 6.30, so we'll have two breaks, and I suggest that we will try to keep them as short as possible. Yes. Any preliminaries? I see none. Mr. Thayer. One moment. Let me just welcome the witness and also remind him about his obligations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. I hope you had a good rest. We are going to proceed with the direct examination and then we'll start with the series of cross-examinations. Same recommendations to you as yesterday. Continue -- you've done extremely well. Continue to keep your replies as brief and to the point as possible. And secondly, please let me remind you that you are testifying pursuant to a solemn declaration that you made yesterday. You don't need to repeat it today. It still holds good. All right? Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I had one preliminary matter at the Court's pleasure we could take up at the conclusion of Mr. Oric's testimony prior to one of breaks. It just concerns e-court matters, and I don't think we need to do it now, but I do want to alert the Court to just one issue that has arisen and what we're doing about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much time do you require for it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think it will just a couple of moments, Your Honour, just to alert the Court to an issue we're trying to resolve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When we ended yesterday, you had been describing for the Trial Chamber your experiences while parked on a bus in front of the Vuk Karadzic school. When we met last week, did I show you a sketch of Bratunac which you drew for investigators in August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And last week did you identify for me on that sketch the locations of the events which you've just described? Yesterday, that is.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have Exhibit 2094 displayed on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see an image on your screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber without going in any specifics just what that is that's being shown on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the school Vuk Karadzic, the buses where they were parked, the place where I was supposed to be shot at and killed and the place where I got off the bus. Also, the football pitch, some houses, and that is that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is this the sketch that you drew for investigators back in August of 1995 that we reviewed last week, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, looking at the sketch, do you see or can you identify where you drew the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school is in front of the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask that with the assistance of the court usher if you take -- there's a special pen connected to that computer, on a cable, and you'll be shown how to use it. If you would just write a number 1 above where you drew the Vuk Karadzic school on that sketch, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could I ask you to -- is it possible to erase an image? Okay. If we could erase the image. And, sir, could you write the number 1 above, above the school, please.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you please draw a number 2 where you drew the entrance to the school, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that you also drew the buses as best you can remember where they were parked. Would you please draw a number 3 to the left of the bus you recall spending that night in.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, it's a little cramped in the sketch, so I'm going to ask you if you can please draw an arrow depicting where your seat on that bus was, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I note for the record that that is the lower right-hand corner of the third rectangle away from the Vuk Karadzic school. It is in a column. Now, would you please mark with an X where you recall the man with some sort of mental disability being shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will object to that. It's obviously leading.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why do you object, Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because the Prosecutor said at the place where he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the witness hasn't actually ever confirmed that he saw that man being shot. He -- I think he ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The objection is sustained, Mr. Krgovic. The witness never said yesterday that he -- he assumes -- he presumes, first, that this person was handicapped, because he doesn't know himself. He was told that. And secondly, that he was shot. They are both presumptions, so let's treat them as such and put questions which would reflect his presumption, but not as a fact, not as an established fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Understood, and I recall the -- the Court's concern about my question yesterday along the same lines. I -- two things, Your Honour. One is I used the word "shot" not "killed" in my question, and yesterday I believe Mr. Oric testified that he observed this group of people around this man and that he recalls a burst of fire and that his recollection is that was the sequence of events with respect to this man. So I'm certainly not trying to imply that he saw who shot the man, but I believe his testimony was clear that he saw -- his conclusion was that the gunfire came from this group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer. Do you see my -- what reaction you caused? Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 82, line 12.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter missed the first part of Madam Fauveau's intervention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau, I understood what you said but it is completely missing from the transcript. If you could you repeat, please, your indication and what -- your comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said yesterday, line 82 -- page 82, line 12, that he heard a shot. He never said that he saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I object to the Prosecutor summarising the evidence as he is. There was an objection made. You sustained it, and instead of moving on now he's summarising the evidence, and I believe that's improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Meek. Any further remarks? I suggest you comply with our ruling, Mr. Thayer, and not argue about it. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you would, sir, do you recall the last area where you saw this individual who you were told had mental disabilities before he was dragged away towards the school? Can you mark that on the sketch, please, with an X?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I see that you've drawn a mark on top of one of the rectangles.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him at the door when they were dragging him out. That was the last time I saw him. I did not actually see him being dragged on the ground. The last time I saw him was as he was being dragged out of the bus at the bus door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, do you understand any English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Very well. But can you read English and understand it, or at least a few words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if you look at that diagram that you have in front of you, to the right of where you put that X, where you have another box with the words "Kuc," there are some words in English there. Can you read them and understand what they say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Streetlight."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What does "streetlight" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And above those words are other words. Can you read those words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm taking your word, and I close this chapter with you here. However, it's not closed to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: With any other -- I think you know exactly where I'm heading. With any other witness that could understand what there is written in -- in -- in English over there, or it could be in any other language or even his own language, that would be suggesting to the witness the answer he's supposed to give once you indicate that particular spot to him during the -- your examination, and we don't want that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that this is his own diagram, but certainly what is written in English is not his own making, not his own doing. That's yours. So we -- you could have used a diagram which he created himself without any additions and let him explain rather than have one with ready-made or ready-prepared answers which, if not this one, some other witness could follow. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, you're absolutely correct. This document is his own sketch. We reviewed it with him in his own language. It was never my understanding that he understood any written English, but it is his document. We understand the Court's concerned about suggestivity about marks on documents whether they're maps or sketches, but given that it was his sketch that's been shown to him before. He identified it as such. We felt that this complies with the Court's previously stated concern about doing that. We understand the Court's concern, and we will certainly comply with that as we proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I mean to say is, he's now marked an X in red, or it shows up in red on our monitor. Previously on that diagram or on that sketch there is already another X in black, and from that X there is a line which then leads to the words "Retarded man shot." They are in English. There is no corresponding words in Serbo-Croat there. So if what he did was just a marking, he should have left it at that and not put "Retarded man shot" now and face him with a simple question. I mean, he didn't read out or pronounce "streetlight" in any different manner than anyone who knows English would pronounce it. Again, I'm not doubting his affirmation, but this should not be the practice that you should be following. I mean, we are not taking this matter any further because, as agreed, this is his own sketch. But again there are indications which are just in English and not just the translation of what he himself wrote, like "standena egrada," which is translated apartment building, but this is something which he did not write.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's understood, Your Honour. Unfortunately this is the document he drew in August of 1995, and it is a very -- as we will argue, is a very accurate drawing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not -- that's beside the point, Mr. Thayer. That's beside the point. The practice should have been -- you should have had two documents, one for your own purposes indicating the various sites, and one being his original diagram, and anything else inserted or included, added to what he himself drew up should be kept apart, especially additions are indications of what is shown on the sketch itself. But anyway, let's close at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed. But I think you've got our message. Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. For a point of clarification, previously there was an arrow drawn by this witness which is now missing from this exhibit, Exhibit 2094. There was an arrow drawn to -- when they asked him which seat on the bus were you sitting in, and he had drawn an arrow. It's now missing, okay? Number two, my second point for clarification, we don't know who yet has filled in these boxes. For example, the witness has testified that he last saw this supposedly retarded man sitting inside the bus yet the X is on the outside of the bus. Three, we don't know, we are certain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think these are matters you can raise on cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour we did notice that arrow has disappeared and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps you can ask him to put it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes. We'll just ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you would indicate again where you recall your seat being located on that bus and if you would do that by drawing an arrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Actually, the arrow is still there, Mr. Thayer. It's only the x superimposed part of it. Let's proceed, please, because we're getting stuck here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. The-may I just ask whether the arrow is in fact there because I can't see it on my screen. So if I So if I could have some confirmation that the arrow is actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, there are two arrows now. One is the one that Mr. Meek couldn't see any more, and it's still there. And the other one is now towards the other end of the bus so that makes matters a little bit more confused because if before we had an indication of where the rear of the bus could be, now the bus has got two rears, one in front and one in the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified that there was a streetlight in the area of your bus. Would you draw a circle in the area where you recall that streetlight being located.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were none either in front of my bus or around it. There was streetlight behind the bus, somewhere around here, in this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, as I understand it, the e-court procedure is, as we've finalised the changes that we need to save this somehow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm speaking for myself. I understand that this diagram of his own drawing. That said, do we need to spend time to ask him to mark on his own painting again?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand that concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We spent already half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The -- my intention was to move quickly through it so that he would be able to explain the document and demonstrate to the Court that his knowledge, his recollection is actually current and it's not just something that he wrote back in August of 1995 and no longer recalls as fresh recollection. That is why I wanted to actually go with him so he could show the Court that he recalls from this diagram based on his memory drawing this diagram and this is where the various events occurred, to help place in a pictorial sense for the Court how these and where these events occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I didn't intend it to take this long. Had I known we would have run into some of these obstacles I may have reconsidered that decision but here we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whose write is there in B/C/S, Skola Vuk Karadzic, VK. Is this his writing or someone else's?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand the question of His Honour? Where it is written "Skola VK," whose handwriting is that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And while we were at this, what's in English, was it put on the diagram in your presence at the time, and by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was written in 1995 in Tuzla during the interrogation that I underwent. I don't remember who was present from the commission, but they were the ones who wrote it down in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in my presence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified that on the -- that you spent the night of 13 July on that bus. Did you sleep that night?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what you recall happening first on the morning of 14 July?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first thing that happened was that one of the military policemen came and told us that we would soon be heading off to Kladanj. And this is what happened. Shortly we started for Kladanj to be exchanged there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did your bus finally leave the Vuk Karadzic school, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. The last bus started first, and mine was second in the row when we were heading for Konjevic Polje. The others followed, the remaining two buses followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And on your way in the direction of Konjevic Polje, did you -- did your bus make any stops?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stopped at a parking lot of the Vihor company. There was on the left a space called Rakovica. We stopped there, and they said that we were waiting for UNPROFOR. We asked them if we could go out to go to the toilet, to a canal, and they let us go one by one, and we were waiting for UNPROFOR to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me stop you there, sir. Do you recall what kind of company was Vihor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a company that operates buses and trucks, and this is -- this was where they placed the old trucks, garbage.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you -- were you ever told during that period of time at the Vihor company how many other vehicles there were in addition to your buses?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we went out, we saw that two other buses had come and four trucks with canvasses that were parked behind us. I was not able to see what was there because of the canvasses, if there were people, but they were following us, these four trucks. So six buses and four trucks when we headed for Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you've testified about these three military policemen who stayed with you all the way from Konjevic Polje up until Vihor. Were they replaced at some point?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Another smaller truck arrived, and armed men, armed soldiers came out and replaced the military policemen. When they were replaced, an APC arrived on the scene. They greeted each other, and then I was able to see that these were not men from -- UNPROFOR men but Serbian soldiers, because they greeted each other by holding up three fingers. They headed first and then we followed. We were heading for Kladanj to be exchanged there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was there anything about that APC that suggested to you that this was, in fact, an UNPROFOR APC, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say that the UNPROFOR carrier is white with UN letters written in black. And I was convinced that it was an UNPROFOR APC, because I used to see them a lot for three years in Srebrenica. I'm a hundred per cent sure that it was an UNPROFOR APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall what these soldiers on the APC were wearing?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blue flak jackets, UNPROFOR flak jackets. They also wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did your convoy finally set off again from the Vihor garage?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. We will set off in the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you testified that the APC led the way. What direction did it head as it travelled that Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This direction leads through Glogova, Kravica, Sandici, Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you reached the intersection at Konjevic Polje that you testified about yesterday, what direction did your bus take?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived at the intersection, the APC turned right. This is the road to Drinjaca and Zvornik. Of course, the buses followed the APC as it turned.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, had you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Thayer. I just want to get this clear in my mind at least. The suggestion of witness is that this last group that arrived, the APC, in other words, it was not UNPROFOR personnel in a UN APC but Serb soldiers in an UNPROFOR APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I just wanted to make sure of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, based on your familiarity with the area and the routes, had you -- had you actually been heading towards Kladanj for exchange, which direction should you have turned at that intersection at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we were heading for Kladanj, we would have gone left to Kasaba, Miljevici [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I notice that the transcript said "Miljevici" a second ago. Is that correct or was it some other town or location that you wish to mention?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. M-i-l-e-c-i [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you pronounce that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber the route that the bus you were in, in the convoy took? And I would just note that I do plan to use a map with Mr. Oric to assist the Court in demonstrating the route followed from Bratunac to Zvornik. I will get there. He's going to describe it first and then we'll use the map. So, sir, will you describe where you recall the bus going once you took that turn right at Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we started towards Zvornik, from Konjevic Polje to Drinjaca there is a place where there are rocks on either sides. At this spot we were ordered to bow our hands in between our legs, to cover our eyes with our hands, and not to watch in order not to see where we were being -- where we were being taken, and that's how we proceeded towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you able to see at all where the bus was going, sir, despite that order?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I saw everything. I peaked through my fingers. I saw Drinjaca, Zvornik, Karakaj as we were passing by. We turned left towards Kalesija to Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then where did your bus head after that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction Karakaj-Kalesija. We didn't travel for a long time. The bus turned right again, and shortly after that the buses stopped. As I was peeking through the fingers, we saw that we arrived in a hamlet where there was a school and a monument in front of the school. We turned there and they told us that we could raise our heads and to run out of the bus and to run towards the school. The first bus was emptied, and then we were told to run towards the school, and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you able to see anything else about that school during -- from the period of time your bus arrived at the school until the time you ran off the bus?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to see there was a monument in front of the school next to the road, and I saw a football pitch that we ran across. There was also -- there was a net which prevented the ball from being thrown out of the pitch on the left and on the right side. I also saw there were buildings around. This is what I was able to see as I was running towards the school and while I was still seated on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You referred to a football pitch, sir. What was that football pitch made of?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concrete. It was a concrete pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you also observe any vehicles in the area when your bus arrived?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only the APC, which led the way. It had parked on the side, and one of the soldiers was sitting on top of it. And then I was able to see also the convoy that had followed the APC and the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: While you were running into the school, were you being guarded by any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers on either side, on the left and on the right, of the pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you allowed to bring anything into the school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we weren't. It was very hot on the bus, so people took off their coats or their sweaters and they held them in their hands. We had to leave it. There was a small meadow on the right-hand side between the school and the staircase, and that's where we had to leave our belongings. People who had berets also had to take them off and throw them there, and that's when we entered the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were your belongings or your group's belongings were the first items deposited there, or did there already appear to be items in that area?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were other items that I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Before we continue into the next events, Mr. President, I'd like to review the map notice same manner that we did yesterday, at the Court's suggestion. If I may hand this to the court usher to place on the ELMO. This is map 5 of the map book. Our focus is a little off. I don't know about everybody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's everybody's. I mean, that is something that can be taken care of, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could please zoom in a little bit. I don't know if that would help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I would stop there for the time being so we have Bratunac at the extreme right. And if we could perhaps improve a little bit on the focusing. No, no. Focusing, not -- I mean, zoom out. Zoom out. Stop there. Stop there. And it's the focusing that is not good.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May I ask if everyone has adequate focus at this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mine is out of focus anyway, but I don't know if I am being understood. This is usually a problem that is easily solved. I'm told this is the best they can do. Thank God for e-court, because we would have had it better. I don't know what's happening. Anyway, we can more or less distinguish the names, so let's not lose more time. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you -- you testified a moment ago that the route followed Bratunac, you mentioned Glogova and Kravica. Do you see those landmarks represented on this map?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. We're hearing music through our.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So am I. It's gone. I was going to say, sad old story again. Let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you trace by stating the name of the towns that you view on this map your route as your bus left Bratunac, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you just name the towns that are located on the town in front of you in the order that you remember seeing them on your journey from Bratunac to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we shorten it? Can he just indicate along the map, and then I just make an entry for the record which route he has indicated, whether it's the one which goes to Karakaj or whether it's the one which goes to Kladanj or Milici? Let's -- go ahead. With the pointer, follow the road that you went on that day.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We need now to lower down -- yes. Further down, madam. A little bit further down. Yes. Stop. We had arrive at Konjevic Polje. So if you could continue from there, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So for the record, the witness pointed to the road which from Bratunac leads first to Konjevic Polje, then to Karakaj, and finally to Orahovac, and indicating also the following villages: Glogova, Kravica, Sandici, Karakaj, and Orahovac. Konjevic Polje in the middle. Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Returning to the school, sir, after you deposited the remaining items that you had, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came to the hallway, and then we headed left towards the gym. We entered in a small hall, small room, something resembling a locker room, and then we entered the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did you see when you entered the gym?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a bigger group of people at the end of the hall which had arrived prior to our arrival, and they were from the bus that was emptied first. They were sitting at the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you estimate for the Trial Chamber approximately how many people you saw in the gym when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Thayer. I hate to interrupt you again, but in lines 11 and 12 he mentions a small hall. Now, this is something which he certainly distinguishes from the gym, which he refers to on page -- in line 13. Then you put a question which is, of course, understandably the correct one, "What, if anything, did you see when you enter the gym?" But then he doesn't say, "In the gym I saw the following." He said, "I saw a bigger group of people at the end of the hall."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I just want to make sure. I think he refers to the gym, as I understand it. I just want to make sure that he does, and I just don't want confusion with the hall in a hall, in other words, as from the gym. If you could put the question to him, please. In which part of the building did he see those others that had arrived previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, when you entered the school, you testified that you saw a group of individuals that you testified were taken off one of the prior buses. What part of the building were those persons located in?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were located in the gym or sports hall at the rear. They were taken off first, and that's how we were seated in the sports hall, in the gym, from the bottom towards the entrance. This was not -- they were not from one bus. I think that they had arrived before. It was a substantial group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you say bottom, do you mean from the far end of the hall as you were facing it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the far end of the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, how exactly were you instructed to position yourselves once you were inside the gym?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we were entering, we sat down. As the busloads of people entered, the area became more and more crammed, so they ordered us to sit tighter to each other, and if we didn't -- if we hadn't done that, they would have shot at us. And they asked us to put our knees below our chins. They ordered us to do that, and they said that if we didn't do that they would shoot at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how long prisoners continued to arrive inside the gym?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened really fast, because we were running. One part of the hall was not full at first, but maybe 10, 15, or 20 minutes later new people started arriving, and -- and then the situation was crazy. We had to push each other in order to all fit in. The room was completely full. The hall was bursting at the edges.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At some point were you instructed to reconfigure yourselves?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When a man came, I suppose he was and commander, he was tall, had dark hair, had sunglasses, and he instructed us to face the wall. The first four rows to face the wall, then the four rows to turn right, the next four rows to turn left, and it went on like that. At the end some of people were facing the walls. Some of the people had their backs turned to the wall. Some were turned left. The others were turned right. I was somewhere in the middle of the hall, and I was facing the entrance into the sports hall, the door that we had come through. That's how he regrouped us. That's how he reconfigured us.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you estimate, sir, how many prisoners were placed in the gym while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the size of the sports hall and by the way we were seated, I would say that there were over 2.000 of us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately what time of day you arrived at the gym?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't have a watch. I believe it was around noon. This is when we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was the temperature like inside the gym, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was terrible. It was hot outside. It was in July. So people started fainting, the elderly particularly. Only there was no way to fall. You just saw them hang with their heads hanging on their shoulders and you knew that they had fainted. It happened to all the elderly people, all those who were over 70. They were the ones who had fainted. And nobody could help them. We didn't dare stand up to help them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And why was there no way to fall, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were all seated with our knees below our chins and there was just no room to fall. We were all squeezed tight. There was just no way for them to turn over, to lie down.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were there any boys being held in the gym, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw some. I believe three or four. There may have been even more. Later on, these boys would bring water to us. They had been given buckets, and these children brought us water. I saw four of them. I don't know how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was everyone able to get water, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The far end of the sports hall could not get hold of water because these boys, when they brought water they would reach only the centre of the sports hall, then the buckets would be emptied. They would return, they would start the process all over again. The far end of the sports hall did not stand a chance. People were thirsty. And by the time the boys reached the middle of the sports hall, all the water would be gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, we'll have a break in five minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could you describe the effect of the heat on you during your time in that gym, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I almost fainted. My cousin Haris, who was with me all the time, he was providing me with comfort. He was encouraging me. It -- I was very little short of fainting myself, because the temperature and the anxiety that reigned in the room was unbearable. It was very hard to breathe because your knees were under your chin, and this prevented you from breathing properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: During the entire time that you were in this gym, sir, was anyone offered or given any medical attention?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How about food?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see any of the prisoners being removed from the gym, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw one man who had lost it from the heat and from the -- from people being squeezed. He stood up, although they had told us, "Don't stand up, we'll shoot." And he still stood up and shouted, "Don't be afraid, people. There is enough of us." The commander came, said, "Who said that?" He wouldn't do that. And the commander said, "Push him out or we'll shoot at you." So people pushed him out, and at the very exit from the sports hall the guards shot at him and killed him, and they dragged his body away. And then they shouted at us asking us, "Is there anybody else who wants to say something like that?" And we all kept quiet. We didn't dare say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just stop you right there, and I'll have just a couple of more questions on this issue before we break. You testified a moment ago that the commander came and said, "Who said that," and then the transcript indicates that you testified, "He wouldn't do that." When you stated, "He wouldn't do that," can you explain to the Trial Chamber what you meant, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said the commander who was in charge there, he issued orders to the soldiers. He asked as follows: "Is there anybody else who shares this man's opinion?" If that is what you're asking me. Was that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No. Going back a few moments ago when you were describing exactly what transpired once the commander, the person you identified as the commander came in, the transcript indicates, "He wouldn't do that." When you said, "He wouldn't do that," who is the "he" you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. I said the commander entered the sports hall and ordered us to push that person out, because after having been ordered to come out himself, the man wouldn't do that. So the commander ordered the rest of us to push him out or else he would shoot at all of us, and that's why people pushed that man out, and that's where -- when they shot at him and killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think this is our break time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Oric, we will have a 20-minute break. Please, everybody try to be as punctual as possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall any high-level Serb officers arriving at the gym, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one point I was talking to my cousin, and I heard somebody say, "There's Mladic." I lifted my head, and we saw him in the corridor at the entrance to the sports hall. He was talking to the man with the sunglasses. He was observing what was going on in the sports hall. He stayed there maybe a couple of minutes, or maybe three or four minutes, and then left. He went away from that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What happened to you next, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After some time, I don't know how long, the man with the sunglasses, the commander who was there, told us to prepare ourselves to leave because we were being taken to the Batkovici camp. He forbade us to stand up. He told us to head towards the door on the right-hand side in the seated position. And after the door there was a room, something like a locker room, and there was an exit there, an exit that led outside. There were some wooden grills there that must have been used in the sports hall for training. We prepared ourselves, and we thought we would be taken to the Batkovici camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Did the name "Batkovici camp" have any significance to him at the time, or to the ones who were with him? At least as far as location is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you understand the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the Batkovici camp in Bijeljina, which was a well-known camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, when you say "camp," what kind of camp are you describing?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A camp where detained Bosniaks were kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What was your understanding of what the prisoners at this camp -- what eventually happened to them, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What was your understanding of the purpose of this camp at Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were told that we would be taken to the Batkovici came be, we didn't think we would fare badly because that camp was a registered camp, and from there we could be exchanged or something. However, when they placed tables at the exit and when they brought some boxes and buckets with water, the first people who went out were first blindfolded. They were given a cup of water to drink, and then they were taken outside, and this is how it kind. Then we started being suspicious. We didn't know why their eyes were being blindfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me stop you right there, sir. Would you please describe for the Trial Chamber the process by which yourself and the other prisoners in that gym were removed from the gym.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When -- when these tables were placed outside, two men were taken from the sports hall. I knew one of them. Mezir Gusic is his name. He was the one who blindfolded the others. We were not allowed to stand up. We crawled to at that place and then we were ordered to stand up. Then we would be blindfolded, given a cup of water to drink and then we would be taken to the truck and that's how it went on until my turn came with the sixth group of people. Five groups came before me. I went with the sixth group of people that were ordered to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me stop you there, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record, to line 5 on page 29, is it Mezir -- if he could repeat the name again, please, the person who was blindfolding the others.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mezir Gusic, G-u-s-i-c.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe the area in which this blindfolding took place? Was it part of the gym or was it a separate area, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already told you, this was a small room in the middle of the hall to the right-hand side. It was something like a small locker room separated from the sports hall, and this is where we were blindfolded, and from there we were taken onto the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In this locker room area, were there any other Serb soldiers, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the left corner there was a woman, a young woman in a camouflage uniform holding an automatic rifle ready to shoot, and there were four or five other armed soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could clarify with this witness the meaning of soldiers. And also, I wonder whether the witness has described in detail about the commander, except for the fact that he had dark hair and sunglasses. So given his career, I think he should be familiar with military things. So what he wore and what he looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Gladly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to the commander whom you described earlier who appeared at the gym, can you offer the Court any more detail regarding his appearance, any uniform or any other distinctive apparel that would suggest his rank or detachment or any other information about -- about him?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The person whom I perceived as and commander did not enter the sports hall. He stayed at the entrance to the sports hall. He was about two metres tall. He wore a black uniform, not a camouflage uniform. He had black sunglasses and dark hair. An oval face. I did not see his patches or his rank because he did not come any closer to me. So I wouldn't be able to tell you his rank. However, judging by the way he commanded everybody else, he was in charge there. He issued orders to the other Serb soldiers who were there. He told them what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you estimate approximately how far you were seated from the entrance to the -- to the gym?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the middle of the sports hall. I don't know how far that is in metres from the entrance. I couldn't measure the sports hall, so I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, with respect to the soldiers whom you testified were in this locker room area while you were being blindfolded, were you able to distinguish any identifying information from their appearance with respect to what unit, or brigade, or what element of the military they were attached to?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not able to see that, and I can't tell you. As one stood up, one would be blindfolded and taken to the truck. I didn't manage to see anything, and I wouldn't be able to tell you what unit they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Coming back to Judge Kwon's question. On what basis does he state that they were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't see the patches, but they wore camouflage uniforms, and they wore arms. I didn't see any markings of their belonging, what unit they belonged to, but judging by the camouflage uniforms they wore and the weapons they carried, they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Caps by any chance?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were these people you identified as soldiers wearing any head-gear of any kind?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't have anything on their heads. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, can you describe for the Trial Chamber, please, your experience as you were being blindfolded at the gym. What did you hear? What did you observe?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They only told us not to push too much and that nobody should stand up, and that was that. And if you're asking me what we were talking about amongst each other, then I can tell you that we were discussing as to whether we would really be taken to the camp or we would be killed. We were really suspicious about those blindfolds. We were thinking if we were being taken to the camp why were we blindfolded? I don't remember anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, were the prisoners called up and kept in groups or was it just one at a time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One at a time. And as we approached the door, we went out. There was no way for anybody from the rear to skip the file. We were not allowed to stand up before our time came. And people were not called either by names or by groups. We just left the sports hall single file.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you estimate approximately how many other people -- how many other prisoners were nearby you while you were waiting and blindfolded?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Close to me were my relatives and neighbours whom I knew. Next to me was Nurif Hodzic. There was also Ehrem Hasanovic, Haris Hasanovic, my relatives. There was also Hakija and Eso Malic, a father and son. And we agreed if we were taken to Batkovici to stay together, not to separate. We tried to exit in one group, and that's how we managed to exit the sports hall together although some people were added to our group. In any case, 12 or 13 people would be put on one truck. Then we waited for the next truck to come. But the whole process was very fast, and the lorries returned very fast, and we were not clear about that. We didn't know how these lorries could return so fast if we were near Zvornik. It was not near Bijeljina, so there was no way for these trucks to return so fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How do you know that these lorries were returning, sir, if you were blindfolded?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because -- I don't know. I gathered there could not be that many lorries all together. We heard a lorry leaving and then another coming. We could hear the lorries leaving and arriving and pulling away and parking, and I gathered that. Their numbers was just very high.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And by the way, do you recall who actually gave you your blindfold?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mezir Gusic was the one who blindfolded us. A native of Krizevci in Srebrenica municipality. He blindfolded us. When I stood up, I asked him, "What do you think? Where are we being taken?" My eyes were full of tears [as interpreted], and he told me, "I don't know." He blindfolded me. Somebody grabbed my arm. I stepped onto the lorry, and I could see below my blindfold that there was a huge tyre on the lorry. I passed that tyre. There were benches on both sides of the lorry. I sat down, and my relatives came after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just stop you there, sir. The transcript indicates that you asked Mr. Gusic, "What do you think? Where are we being taken?" And your testimony was, "My eyes were full of tears." Is that a correct statement, that your eyes were full of tears, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, his eyes. His eyes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. That question has been asked and answered. It's repetitive and there's no reason for the Prosecutor to ask that question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: His answer is sufficient proof that it was really needed because it has clarified the previous transcript. So let's move ahead, Mr. Thayer. Thank you, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall exactly which of your relatives were next to you inside this lorry, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those that I just mentioned. Haris Hasanovic, Edhem Hasanovic, Esad Hakija, the father and son. Nurif Hodzic. They were together with me and there were some other people who joined us, but I didn't know them. They filled up our lorry with some more people whom I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: One you were inside the lorry, sir, did you have any interaction with any of those relatives whom you just described?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sports hall my relative had an opportunity to -- to exchange a few words with the Serb soldiers. I didn't see well. I suppose that he was asking for a cigarette. But when we were in the lorry, he told me, "Here, have a cigarette." He -- I suppose he lit the cigarette in the lorry. He was going to give me the cigarette. I lifted my blindfold to take the cigarette, and I saw that there was a red car after us, and there was a Serb soldier with a rifle looking through the window. He told me to return the blindfold. I did that. The tarpaulin was open in the back so he could see me from the car. I replaced my blindfold and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And which relative did you have this interaction with concerning the cigarette, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Haris Hasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Approximately how long did it take to arrive at your destination, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately four or five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you please describe for the Trial Chamber what happened once you arrived.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in that place, when the lorries pulled over, they told us to jump out and to hurry up. We jumped out. The lorry was not that high. It was a small tonne lorry. And when we jumped out I saw under the blindfold I was jumping onto a meadow. My relative called me. He jumped out of the lorry. I turned around, and then at the asked us to line up. I suppose we were in one compact group. I took my relative by the hand, and he told me, "They're going to kill us." I said, "No, they're not. Don't fret." And that's when bursts of fire started. The lorries left, and they started shooting at us. My relative was killed immediately. He was screaming, and he was squeezing my hand very tight. I pushed his hand, and I threw myself on the ground. And he fell on me, on the lower side of my back, and from that moment on I pretended I was dead. He was shaking. His body was shaking on my body, and then he went stiff. He died on me. And the rest of the group, maybe two or three of them, started wailing and screaming because they were wounded, and these other men came and finished them off. And that's how it continued. People were being brought there and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, were you injured by the gunfire, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You indicated that there were -- that it continued, that people were brought and killed. How were you able to make at that conclusion, sir, that that was going on?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I concluded by the arrival of the lorries and the same words, "Line up," and then bursts of fire and then wounded people screaming and being finished off. And this continued. This went on. And -- and I could -- I could feel bullets flying above me. I was afraid that one of them might hit me and injure me. And they lined these people in front of our group, and people kept falling, and I could hear all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you hear the Serb soldiers saying anything during this process?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If somebody was wounded, they would call him by the name Zulfo, and they would say, "There you have another Zulfo twirling and twisting," and I would hear shots after that. There were people who were asking them, "Kill me." And then they would curse them, and they would say, "Suffer some more, you Ustasha," or, "you Muslim." Sometimes they would not finish those people off immediately but they would let them suffer in agony for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, was "Muslim" the word that they -- that they used, that you heard them use, or was it another word?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Zulfo" is a Muslim name, and they used that name the most. Zulfo was the person who finished off the wounded. They would call him, this Zulfo by name, and they would tell him, "Zulfo, there is another one who is not dead."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Other than the lorries that -- that you heard, did you hear any other vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I was lying on the ground, to my right-hand side I could hear the engines that were in the middle of doing something. I could hear the sound of these engines.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Based on the sound of the engine did you have any idea of what kind of engines you were hearing?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the sound, I could tell that those were bigger engines. And when I stood up and when I looked at them, I saw that those were construction machines that are used to excavate and load material onto lorries.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll get to that in a few minutes, sir. Can you estimate for the Trial Chamber how long the process of the lorries arriving and the shooting continued?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember up to the moment when some people started running away. One tried to start away across the forest. They shot after him. And another one jumped up behind their backs and ran away. They did not manage to kill the latter one. They said that they would ambush him somewhere and kill him. One of them cursed God and said, "You did not do the job properly. You have to finish them off by shooting in their heads," and that's what they did. They went from one to the next. And when they came up to me, this person shot into my relative's head. At that moment, I -- either I had dozed off or I had fainted, but from that moment on I can't remember a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall until approximately what time of day you remember the executions lasting?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly, but this was sometime in the afternoon, maybe around 1.00 or 2.00 in the afternoon. I don't know exactly. The sun was high, so this may have been sometime in the afternoon, early afternoon. Between 1.00 and 3.00, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think the answer is clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm going there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If the -- Mr. Thayer, I mean you're closer to the witness. If he needs a short break, we'll give him a short break.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, please, at any time if you feel you need to take a break, I'm sure the Trial Chamber will accommodate your request, but feel free to let us know, and we will do that. Are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you estimate for the Trial Chamber how long during the course of that afternoon, during the course of at that day, you recall these executions lasting while you were playing dead?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This took some time, maybe an hour or so. They kept on bringing people, and then I fainted. From the moment I fell onto the ground and started playing dead until the moment I fainted, I believe that this lasted for an hour. And all that time we were bringing people there and killing them. Maybe it lasted less than that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You said that at some point you fainted. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what you recall after that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was already late afternoon when I woke up. There -- it was raining. I was half naked. I didn't have a shirt on. It started raining. I believe the rain woke me up. And then I took my blindfold off. It was already. I could see lights. I was lit. I didn't dare lift my head. I continued lying on the ground. They continued bringing people in, but I could also hear people being taken off the trucks saying, "Don't kill us. We are not guilty of anything." It was already dark when this was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you able to tell what the source of the light was that shone on you when you awoke?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably those big machines that were working there shone their lights on me. When I stood up, I saw a loader machine, an excavator, and I suppose I had been shone by those machine. Maybe previously there was something else that had its lights turned on and then it left, but I did see an excavator with its lights on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to be clear. When you first came to in the rain, you testified that you took your blindfold off. Did you stand up at that point or at some other point?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I took my blindfold off ever so slowly, I didn't dare lift my head. I did not lift my head let alone stand up. I remained lying on the ground, and I could see that I was lit up. That's why I didn't dare stand up, because they would see me immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you please pick up with your recollection of what happened after that point.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, the killing went on. I don't know for how long. At one point I heard somebody saying -- first a vehicle came, and when that vehicle could be heard, there was no killing. There was no shooting. And then I heard somebody saying, "That's it. We've finished. We have to leave somebody behind." And they started arguing amongst themselves and saying that there is no need for anybody to stay on because we were all dead, that they had to go somewhere and rest and that the following morning they would throw our bodies into the grave. They turned the engines off, and they -- then I heard them leaving. I stayed on the ground for maybe 10 or 15 minutes more. I was listening to see whether somebody had been left behind and that this was not just some sort of tactic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me stop you right there, sir. During this -- these conversations that you overheard, do you recall what words, if any, they were using to describe the dead prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They used derogatory words. They were cursing. They said, "Fuck them. They're all dead. There's no need for us to stay." This is what they were saying amongst each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was there a particular derogatory word they were using to refer to the dead prisoners, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day while I was still conscious, they used the words Turk to refer to us. They said fuck our Turk mothers, and they said we were best off dead. A lot of things were being said while I was still conscious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I better interrupt you here because otherwise I'll forget it. One thing that we've not heard from the witness is the following: During the time when he was conscious and he was hearing the arrival of lorries or trucks, the shooting, and then the departure of lorries, fresh arrival, et cetera, can he be precise or as precise as possible as to the frequency of arrivals? How often? You said it lasted maybe one hour before you lost consciousness.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you understand the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: During that hour that these lorries or trucks were arriving or going, arriving or going, how frequently would one truck follow the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. Maybe every four or five minutes. The same way I arrived the others arrived every four or five minutes, and I'm claiming that they used two trucks. One would bring people while the other was being loaded at the other end. So the whole process was very fast. Every four or five minutes a truck would come, people would get off, be killed, the lorry would return, and this continued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also understood you to say before that when you regained consciousness, arrival of trucks and shooting continued to take place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And did the arrival of trucks now in the late evening -- was it having the same frequency as before? Were they arriving every four or five minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And how long did that last before -- until you did not hear any further shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, again, this repeated every four or five minutes, but this time round people already knew what was going on, and people cried and begged not to be killed. And this lasted for another hour or so, then then finally that vehicle appeared and I could hear the words, "That's it. Finished."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified that after you heard the soldiers leave the area you waited a little while. Can you please pick up from that point and tell the Trial Chamber what happened next.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 10 or 15 minutes, I tried to move but my body was numb. So first I tried to move my arms. Then I lifted myself to my knees. I removed the body of my cousin off me. I stood up. It was partly clouded. You could see the moonlight. And when I saw the meadow filled with bodies, I was very much afraid, and I tried to -- and I started to cry. I couldn't stop. Somebody asked me if I was wounded. I thought myself it's either a ghost or a Serbian soldier. I didn't realise there was anybody else alive there. I saw the person was not shooting, so I concluded that it was somebody who was alive, and I started -- I headed towards that person. It was difficult to reach him because there was a lot of blood. It was very slippery, and I had to walk over bodies. I came up to him. I asked him if he was wounded. He replied that he wasn't. To our right side on the side, two other persons started crying out and moaning in pain. I came up to them and I saw that both of them were wounded. They were riddled with bullets, one of them in the stomach area and the other one in the legs. One of them was -- didn't have his shirt and said he was cold. So I took a shirt off a body and I put it on him. I told them that I couldn't help them, that I couldn't carry them because I could barely walk myself. So they said, "Okay, run away. If you can't help us, run away." He asked for a shoe which was under one of the bodies. And these where we set off. We were going through a graveyard through a forest we didn't know where we were going. There was a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me stop you, sir. You said he asked for a shoe. When you say "he" asked for a shoe, to whom are you referring?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about Hurem Suljic who is one of the survivors. He told me that was his name. Hurem Suljic from Suceska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is that the man you saw after you were able to stand up?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, before you and Mr. Suljic were able to leave the meadow did you see anything on the meadow?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw the pit, the grave that was dug out, and behind we could see the excavator and the loader. The excavator and the loader. They're these two machines. And the grave was very deep. No one could get out. I think it was more than five metres deep.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you estimate how long that pit was, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I think over 10 metres, maybe even more. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask you some questions about this machinery that you saw next to the pit. As you were escaping the meadow, do you recall whether the lights on the machinery at that time were on or off?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When -- when we were running out, running away, the lights were turned off.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you remember drawing a sketch of those machines? Are you okay, sir? Do you need a break, or are you okay to continue?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, we'll have break in less than 20 minutes' time, at ten past 5.00. I'm telling you this so he can hear it as well. If he refers to have the break now, we can have the break now. So it's up to you, Mr. Oric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember drawing a sketch of the two machines that you described previously for the Trial Chamber, drawing a sketch back in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And last week in my office do you remember reviewing that -- that sketch with me?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we display Exhibit 2093 on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you see an image on your screen, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And may I just confirm that that screen is on everyone's screen? I see nods yes. Very well, sir. Is this the sketch that you drew for investigators, sir, back in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And looking at the vehicle on the left, can you describe what that vehicle is and what it does?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This vehicle on the left is a machine used in construction works, which is used for digging very deep. So it digs out -- it digs out soil.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the vehicle on the right, what is that vehicle, sir? What does that do?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The vehicle on the right is also a machine used in construction works, which is used for loading. It has two functions. It can load the soil or fill in.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you drew this sketch back in 1995, did you know these two vehicles by any manufacturer name?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the manufacturer, but I know that they're used in construction works and that they were probably manufactured in Serbia. I don't know the exact make.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you refer to those machines by any other term or general term, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The drawing on the right is referred to as ULT. It's an abbreviation. The one on the left is an excavator. Of course, some companies manufacture motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, the transcript is not picking up the last portion of your answer, and I unfortunately didn't hear it either. You said that some companies manufacture motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They manufacture engines and motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
